He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Oklahoma State Cowboys basketball|Oklahoma State Cowboys]]. ==Early life== McGriff grew up mainly playing [[flag football]]. His parents, Octavia Goodman and Nate McGriff, were separated, with his father working three jobs. He began focusing on basketball as he grew taller and could [[slam dunk|dunk]] by sixth grade.{{cite web |last1=Pfeifer |first1=Ben |title=Stranded in the Deep End: Why Cameron McGriff refuses to quit |url=https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/2020/06/08/stranded-in-the-deep-end-why-cameron-mcgriff-refuses-to-quit/ |publisher=The Rookie Wire |accessdate=June 14, 2020 |date=June 8, 2020}}{{cite web |last1=Ruiz |first1=Nathan |title=Like father, like son |url=https://www.pressreader.com/usa/the-oklahoman/20180214/281861528971048 |website=[[The Oklahoman]] |via=[[PressReader]] |accessdate=June 14, 2020 |date=February 14, 2018}} McGriff attended [[South Grand Prairie High School]] in [[Grand Prairie, Texas]]. As a senior, he averaged 14.3 points and 7.4 rebounds per game.{{cite news |last1=Florek |first1=Michael |title=Boys Regional Basketball Tournament Previews |url=https://www.pressreader.com/usa/the-dallas-morning-news/20160304/284399853265994 |accessdate=June 14, 2020 |work=[[Dallas Morning News]] |date=March 4, 2016}} He was ranked the 10th best recruit in Texas by [[ESPN]] and the No. 113 in his high school class by [[Rivals.com|Rivals]]. McGriff committed to playing college basketball for [[Oklahoma State Cowboys basketball|Oklahoma State]], choosing the Cowboys over [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]] in part because he thought they would help him reach the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]].{{cite news |last1=Riddle |first1=Greg |title=South Grand Prairie basketball stars Cameron McGriff, Harrison Henderson sign with colleges that can produce NBA talent |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/high-school-sports/2015/11/11/south-grand-prairie-basketball-stars-cameron-mcgriff-harrison-henderson-sign-with-colleges-that-can-produce-nba-talent/ |accessdate=June 14, 2020 |work=[[Dallas Morning News]] |date=November 11, 2015}} ==College career== As a freshman, McGriff averaged 3.8 points and 3.1 rebounds in 15.7 minutes per game while showcasing his dunking ability, including a dunk against [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown]] that appeared on [[SportsCenter]]'s Top 10.{{cite news |last1=Hart |first1=Hally |title=McGriff brings poise, maturity to young Cowboy squad |url=https://www.ocolly.com/sports/mcgriff-brings-poise-maturity-to-young-cowboy-squad/article_fd7e902a-e229-11e8-916e-5b3af4f84aed.html |accessdate=June 14, 2020 |website=[[The O'Colly]] |date=November 6, 2018}}{{cite web |last1=Unruh |first1=Jacob |title=OSU basketball: Cam McGriff's role has evolved, but it's soldified his strong legacy |url=https://oklahoman.com/article/5656539/osu-basketball-cam-mcgriffs-role-has-evolved-but-its-soldified-his-strong-legacy |website=[[The Oklahoman]] |accessdate=June 14, 2020 |date=March 4, 2020}} Before his sophomore season, he improved his jump shot, making 1,000 shots each day. As a sophomore, he averaged 8.4 points and 5.4 rebounds per game and helped the team reach the [[National Invitational Tournament]] quarterfinals.{{cite news |title=Oklahoma State Preview Capsule |url=https://apnews.com/675a8e0fd1fb477787f7412904d25cdf |accessdate=June 14, 2020 |work=[[Associated Press]] |date=October 25, 2018}} In November 2018, McGriff scored 28 points in a win against [[LSU Tigers basketball|LSU]].{{cite web |last1=Katz |first1=Andy |title=5 seniors who can have breakout college basketball seasons in 2019-20 |url=https://www.ncaa.com/news/basketball-men/article/2019-05-09/5-seniors-who-can-have-breakout-college-basketball-seasons |website=NCAA.com |accessdate=June 14, 2020 |date=May 10, 2019}} As a junior, McGriff averaged 12.3 points and 7.4 rebounds per game, shooting 38 percent.{{cite news |last1=Bonner II |first1=Frank |title=OSU basketball preview: Cowboys add depth; Cowgirls looking for scorers |url=https://www.tulsaworld.com/sports/college/osu/osu-basketball-preview-cowboys-add-depth-cowgirls-looking-for-scorers/article_52b3bbeb-97b5-5991-9b12-c7caf4082172.html |accessdate=June 14, 2020 |work=[[Tulsa World]] |date=November 2, 2019}} On February 22, 2020, he tied his career-high of 28 points and had seven rebounds in a 83–66 win over [[Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball|Oklahoma]].{{cite news |last1=Bonner II |first1=Frank |title=Cameron McGriff ties his career high in scoring to lead OSU to an 83–66 win over the Sooners |url=https://www.tulsaworld.com/sports/college/osu/cameron-mcgriff-ties-his-career-high-in-scoring-to-lead-osu-to-an-83-66/article_8f8d7b60-c694-544d-8b5b-115bd11b3359.html |accessdate=June 14, 2020 |work=[[Tulsa World]] |date=February 22, 2020}} He averaged 12.3 points and 6.6 rebounds per game as a senior on a team that finished 18–14.{{cite web |last1=Postins |first1=Matthew |title=Oklahoma State Cowboys Basketball 2019-20 Season Review |url=https://www.heartlandcollegesports.com/2020/05/12/oklahoma-state-cowboys-basketball-2019-20-season-review/ |website=Heartland College Sports |accessdate=June 14, 2020 |date=May 12, 2020}} McGriff averaged 19 points per game on the final six games of the season and was named the team's [[most valuable player]] by the ''[[Tulsa World]]''.{{cite news |last1=Bonner II |first1=Frank |title=OSU season in review: The MVP. The highs and lows. What to look for next season |url=https://www.tulsaworld.com/sports/college/osu/osu-season-in-review-the-mvp-the-highs-and-lows-what-to-look-for-next/collection_a964f40b-9332-5d17-91ca-3aca32847457.html#2 |accessdate=June 14, 2020 |work=[[Tulsa World]] |date=March 24, 2020}} He was also named All-[[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] Honorable Mention.{{cite news |last1=Bitterman |first1=Abby |title=Big 12 men's basketball: 3 Sooners and 2 Cowboys receive All-Big 12 honors |url=https://oklahoman.com/article/5656974/big-12-mens-basketball-3-sooners-and-2-cowboys-receive-all-big-12-honors |accessdate=June 14, 2020 |work=[[The Oklahoman]] |date=March 8, 2020}} ==Professional career== ===Okapi Aalst (2020–2021)=== On June 14, 2020, McGriff signed his first professional contract with [[Okapi Aalst]] of the [[Pro Basketball League]] (PBL) in Belgium.{{cite web|title=Very High Level Rookie Cameron McGriff Naar Okapi|url=https://www.okapiaalstar.be/nieuws/very-high-level-rookie-cameron-mcgriff-naar-okapi/|website=OkapiAalstar.be|publisher=[[Okapi Aalst]]|date=June 14, 2020|access-date=June 14, 2020|language=Dutch|archive-date=June 14, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200614163649/https://www.okapiaalstar.be/nieuws/very-high-level-rookie-cameron-mcgriff-naar-okapi/|url-status=dead}} He left the team after the season after averaging 13.4 points and 4.9 rebounds per game in the PBL.{{cite news|title=Okapi Aalst ziet vijf spelers vertrekken|url=https://www.tvoost.be/nieuws/okapi-aalst-ziet-vijf-spelers-vertrekken-122558|work=TVOOST - Regionaal nieuws uit Oost-Vlaanderen|access-date=August 10, 2021|language=nl-nl}}{{cite news|title=Cameron Mcgriff, Basketball Player|url=https://www.proballers.com/basketball/player/72962/cameron-mcgriff|website=Proballers.com|access-date=August 10, 2021}} ===Greensboro Swarm / Portland Trail Blazers (2021–2022)=== On October 8, 2021, McGriff signed with the [[Charlotte Hornets]],{{cite web|first=Quinton|last=Wash|title=Charlotte Hornets Sign Jalen Crutcher and Cameron McGriff|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/press-releases/charlotte-hornets-sign-jalen-crutcher-and-cameron-mcgriff|website=NBA.com|date=October 8, 2021|access-date=October 8, 2021}} but was waived six days later.{{cite web|title=Hornets Waive Crutcher and McGriff|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/hornets-waive-crutcher-and-mcgriff|website=NBA.com|date=October 14, 2021|access-date=October 15, 2021}} On October 24, he signed with the [[Greensboro Swarm]] as an affiliate player.{{cite web|first=Justin|last=Trujillo|title=Swarm Announce Training Camp Roster And Coaching Staff For 2021-22|url=https://greensboro.gleague.nba.com/news/swarmannouncetrainingcamproster/|website=NBA.com|date=October 24, 2021|access-date=October 24, 2021}} In 14 games, McGriff averaged 10.2 points, 4.9 rebounds and 1.4 assists per game. On December 25, 2021, McGriff signed a 10-day contract with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] via the hardship exception.{{cite news|first=Cody|last=Taylor|title=Trail Blazers to sign Cameron McGriff to 10-day hardship contract|url=https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/2021/12/24/trail-blazers-cameron-mcgriff-10-day-hardship-contract/|work=Rookie Wire|date=December 25, 2021|access-date=December 25, 2021}} He appeared in three games for the Trail Blazers, averaging 4.7 points and 5.0 rebounds per game. On January 2, 2022, McGriff entered the NBA's COVID-19 health and safety protocols.{{cite news|title=Trail Blazers' Cameron McGriff: Enters COVID-19 protocols|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/trail-blazers-cameron-mcgriff-enters-covid-19-protocols/|work=[[CBS Sports]]|date=January 2, 2022|access-date=January 6, 2022}} On January 5, McGriff was reacquired by the [[Greensboro Swarm]].{{cite web|title=2021-22 NBA G League transactions|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=NBA.com|access-date=January 5, 2022}} On January 31, he was suspended for one game without pay for leaving the bench during an altercation between the Swarm and the [[Wisconsin Herd]] two days earlier.{{Cite web |title=Two Greensboro Swarm players suspended |url=https://pr.nba.com/two-greensboro-swarm-players-suspended/ |access-date=November 21, 2022 |website=NBA|date=January 31, 2022 }} ===Capitanes de Arecibo (2022)=== On April 21, 2022, McGriff signed with the [[Capitanes de Arecibo]] of the BSN.{{cite tweet|author=La Guerra del BSN|number=1517216974463541250|title=#BSN OFICIAL: El delantero Cameron Mcgriff es el nuevo refuerzo de los Capitanes de Arecibo hasta la llegada de Gustavo Ayón. En 29 juegos de la G-League promedió 23 min 12.3 pts 6.0 reb y 1.6 asistencias por juego.|user=LaGuerraBSN|date=April 21, 2022|access-date=April 21, 2022}} ===AEK Athens (2022–2023)=== On July 19, 2022, McGriff signed a one-year contract with Greek club [[AEK B.C.|AEK Athens]].{{cite web|title=AEK BC signs McGriff|url=https://www.aekbc.gr/en/articles-4197/aek-bc-signs-mcgriff.htm|website=aekbc.com|date=July 19, 2022 |access-date=August 6, 2022}} On February 27, 2023, McGriff parted ways with the club. He averaged 9.1 points and 4.8 rebounds in domestic competition, as well as 6 points and 3.9 rebounds in the [[Basketball Champions League|BCL]]. ===Le Mans (2023)=== On February 27, 2023, McGriff signed with [[Le Mans Sarthe Basket|Le Mans]] of the French [[LNB Pro A|Pro A]].{{cite web|first=Fersu|last=Yahyabeyoglu|title=Cameron McGriff (ex AEK) joins Le Mans|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Greece/news/795874/Cameron-McGriff-(ex-AEK)-joins-Le-Mans|website=EuroBasket.com|date=February 27, 2023|access-date=February 27, 2023}} ===Memphis Hustle (2023–2024)=== On October 30, 2023, McGriff joined the [[Memphis Hustle]].{{cite web|title=Memphis Hustle announce 2023-24 training camp roster|url=https://memphis.gleague.nba.com/news/memphis-hustle-announce-2023-24-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=October 30, 2023|access-date=November 7, 2023}} ===Indiana Mad Ants (2024)=== On March 5, 2024, McGriff was traded to the [[Indiana Mad Ants]].{{cite web|title=Mad Ants acquire rights to Cameron McGriff in a trade with Memphis|url=https://fortwayne.gleague.nba.com/news/mad-ants-acquire-rights-to-cameron-mcgriff-in-a-trade-with-memphis|website=NBA.com|date=March 5, 2024|access-date=March 5, 2024}} ===Santeros de Aguada (2024)=== On April 9, 2024, McGriff signed with the [[Santeros de Aguada]].{{cite tweet|author=La Guerra del BSN|title=#BSNPR OFICIAL: El delantero Cameron Mcgriff es el nuevo refuerzo de los Santeros de Aguada en sustitución de Jonas Jerebko. Jerebko sale de la franquicia tras sufrir una lesión que lo dejará sin poder jugar de manera indefinida.|number=1777782852865638463|user=LaGuerraBSN|date=April 9, 2024|access-date=April 9, 2024|language=Spanish}} ===Indios de Mayagüez (2024)=== On June 10, 2024, McGriff signed with the [[Indios de Mayagüez (basketball)|Indios de Mayagüez]] after leaving Aguada.{{cite tweet|author=Indios de Mayagüez|title=Los Indios de Mayagüez anuncian la firma de Cameron Mcgriff como refuerzo, mientras se trabaja unos procesos administrativos con Diamond Stone (ya se encuentra con el equipo). Mcgriff, alero de 6' 7" de estatura, vio acción durante esta temporada con los Santeros de Aguada.|number=1800241577547247907|user=IndiosBSNPR|date=June 10, 2024|access-date=August 23,
